Title: A Comparative Study of Translation Bias and Accuracy in Multilingual Large Language Models for Cross-Language Claim Verification
Authors: Aryan Singhal, Vivian Shao, Gary Sun, Ruohong Ding, Jonathan Lu, Kevin Zhu
Research_Question: How do translation strategies (pre-translation vs self-translation) impact LLM accuracy and bias across multilingual fact-checking?
Data_and_Languages: X-Fact (15 languages across 5 language families: Romance, Slavic, Turkic, Indo-Aryan, Kartvelian)
Method_Evaluated: Evaluated LLMs (GPT-4, Llama, etc.) comparing pre-translation vs self-translation against mBERT
Key_Findings: Low-resource languages suffer large accuracy drops due to translation bias; self-translation partially mitigates bias in larger LLMs
Limitations: Treated verification accuracy as monolithic; did not disentangle whether failure was MT corruption vs LLM reasoning; did not propose selective checking cascade
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Closest prior work on translation in X-Fact. Does NOT separate E_trans from E_verif, and does NOT propose selective checking.

Title: XFEVER: Exploring Fact Verification across Languages
Authors: Yi-Chen Chang, Canasai Kruengkrai, Junichi Yamagishi
Research_Question: Can multilingual models verify claims across languages, and does prediction similarity to English improve calibration?
Data_and_Languages: FEVER translated into 6 languages (Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Japanese, Chinese)
Method_Evaluated: Zero-shot and translate-train multilingual NLI baselines (mBERT, XLM-R)
Key_Findings: Multilingual models trail English baselines; calibration can be improved by English prediction consistency
Limitations: Synthetic FEVER claims lack real-world journalistic noise; did not use authentic search snippets or evaluate Hindi
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Evaluates cross-lingual transfer on synthetic claims. Does NOT evaluate authentic news evidence or selective cascades.

Title: XRAG: Cross-lingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Authors: Wei Liu, Sony Trenous, Leonardo F. R. Ribeiro, Bill Byrne, Felix Hieber
Research_Question: How do LLMs perform when user queries are in non-English and retrieved context is English or multilingual?
Data_and_Languages: Recent news articles; cross-lingual QA in multiple languages
Method_Evaluated: Monolingual vs Multilingual cross-lingual retrieval evaluated on frontier LLMs
Key_Findings: Identified response language drift and cross-lingual reasoning bottlenecks as primary failure modes
Limitations: Focuses strictly on generative QA; does not evaluate discrete claim verification or veracity classification
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Benchmarking cross-lingual RAG for QA. Does NOT study claim verification or selective verification cascades.

Title: Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive Question Answering Task
Authors: Leonardo Ranaldi, Barry Haddow, Alexandra Birch
Research_Question: Does translating retrieved non-English passages to English improve generative question answering?
Data_and_Languages: Multilingual QA benchmarks across high- and low-resource languages
Method_Evaluated: CrossRAG: translates retrieved passages into English before generation; compares against tRAG and MultiRAG
Key_Findings: CrossRAG significantly improves generation quality across languages by leveraging English LLM capacity
Limitations: Assumes translation is universally beneficial; does not investigate translation factual distortion or fact verification
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Evaluates translate-then-generate for QA. Does NOT study veracity classification, translation errors, or selective original checking.

Title: All Languages Matter: Understanding and Mitigating Language Bias in Multilingual RAG
Authors: Dan Wang, Guozhao Mo, Yafei Shi, Cheng Zhang, Bo Zheng, Boxi Cao, Xuanang Chen, Yaojie Lu, Hongyu Lin, Ben He, Xianpei Han, Le Sun
Research_Question: How does language bias in dense rerankers affect cross-lingual evidence selection in mRAG?
Data_and_Languages: Multilingual knowledge bases across diverse languages
Method_Evaluated: LAURA: Language-Agnostic Utility-driven Reranker Alignment via debiased subset fine-tuning
Key_Findings: Existing rerankers systematically favor English, suppressing answer-critical non-English evidence
Limitations: Operates at the retrieval/reranker stage; does not address downstream evidence translation or verifier reasoning
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Focuses on reranker retrieval bias. Does NOT investigate verifier reasoning or translation fidelity.

Title: When Scale Meets Diversity: Evaluating Language Models on Fine-Grained Multilingual Claim Verification
Authors: Hanna Shcharbakova, Tatiana Anikina, Natalia Skachkova, Josef van Genabith
Research_Question: How do smaller encoders compare against modern decoder-only LLMs on fine-grained multilingual claim verification?
Method_Evaluated: Compared XLM-R, mT5, Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, Mistral Nemo across zero-shot prompting and fine-tuning
Key_Findings: Smaller specialized encoders (XLM-R) consistently outperform 7B-12B parameter LLMs due to evidence utilization failures in LLMs
Limitations: Did not evaluate cross-lingual evidence translation, translation fidelity, or selective checking
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Evaluates direct multilingual verifiers on X-Fact. Does NOT study translation pipelines or error decomposition.

Title: X-FACT: A New Benchmark Dataset for Multilingual Fact Checking
Research_Question: How challenging is automated fact checking across typologically diverse languages?
Data_and_Languages: 25 languages, 31,189 claims scraped from professional fact-checking websites with search snippets
Method_Evaluated: Multilingual mBERT and XLM-R baselines under in-language and zero-shot transfer
Key_Findings: Cross-lingual transfer is challenging; performance is low across low-resource languages
Limitations: Did not evaluate machine translation pipelines or selective verification cascades
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Created the source dataset used in our study. Does NOT study translation error attribution.

Title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
Authors: Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, et al.
Research_Question: Can language models be combined with non-parametric neural retrieval for open-domain generation?
Method_Evaluated: RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token models coupling DPR with BART
Key_Findings: Substantially improved factual generation and reduced hallucination in open-domain QA
Limitations: Monolingual English only; no cross-lingual or translation dynamics
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Foundational RAG architecture. Does NOT address multilingual translation corruption.

Title: FEVER: A Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
Authors: James Thorne, Andreas Vlachos, Christos Christodoulopoulos, Arpit Mittal
Research_Question: Can systems verify claims against Wikipedia evidence using a 3-way label schema (SUPPORTED, REFUTED, NOT ENOUGH INFO)?
Data_and_Languages: 185,445 synthetic English claims generated from Wikipedia
Method_Evaluated: Pipeline of document retrieval, sentence selection, and RTE classification
Key_Findings: Established the benchmark task formulation and 3-way veracity schema for automated claim verification
Limitations: Synthetic entity perturbations derived from Wikipedia; monolingual English only
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Foundational claim verification task and label schema. Does NOT address cross-lingual evidence translation.

Title: OPUS-MT — Building open translation services for the World
Research_Question: Can modular, open-source neural machine translation models be trained and deployed for hundreds of languages?
Data_and_Languages: OPUS parallel corpora across >500 language pairs (including Helsinki-NLP/opus-mt-hi-en)
Key_Findings: Provides fast, open, reproducible translation pipelines for global languages
Limitations: Translates sentence-by-sentence; prone to named entity and numerical transliteration errors in low-resource pairs
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Source of the translation model used in our pipeline. Does NOT evaluate claim verification.

Title: DeBERTaV3: Improving DeBERTa using ELECTRA-Style Pre-Training with Gradient-Disentangled Embedding Sharing
Authors: Pengcheng He, Jianfeng Gao, Weizhu Chen
Research_Question: Can disentangled attention and replaced token detection improve multilingual transformer representations?
Data_and_Languages: Pretrained on CC100 (100 languages); fine-tuned on multilingual NLI (XNLI)
Key_Findings: Consistently outperforms XLM-R and mBERT across cross-lingual NLI and classification benchmarks
Limitations: Zero-shot cross-lingual transfer retains performance gaps between English and Indo-Aryan languages
Overlap_with_Our_Study: Source of the cross-lingual verifier model used in our study.
